input_prompt: `daily_schedule.py`'s `next_run_after(now, run_hour, run_minute, *, day_length_seconds)` computes the next datetime at `run_hour:run_minute` strictly after `now`. `day_length_seconds` is a caller-injected function returning the REAL number of seconds in a given civil calendar day for the scheduler's timezone -- 86400 normally, but 82800 (23h) or 90000 (25h) on a DST spring-forward / fall-back day. When today's run time has already passed, the current implementation rolls to "tomorrow" by adding a HARDCODED `timedelta(seconds=86400)` instead of calling `day_length_seconds(today)` -- so on a DST transition day the computed next-run lands an hour early or late. Fix `next_run_after` to call `day_length_seconds` (passing the candidate day) to get the correct roll-forward duration instead of the hardcoded 86400. Add a regression test named exactly `test_next_run_after_uses_actual_day_length_across_dst` that injects a `day_length_seconds` stub returning 82800 for the relevant day, calls `next_run_after` with `now` just past today's run time, and asserts the returned datetime is exactly 82800 seconds after today's `run_hour:run_minute` (not 86400).
